text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's independent weekly newspapers The Guardian and Mmegi (The Reporter) on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Botswana Housing Corporation has announced the offer of voluntary retrenchment to 250 workers. The corporation lost 17 million pula last year. The retrenchment programme will cost 8,2 million pula.
- Debts incurred in Botswana by the now Deputy Minister for Safety and Security in South Africa, Joe Matthews, and for which he faced criminal charges, have been paid.

- The Botswana Confederation of Commerce, Industry and Manpower has completed a report on privatisation in Botswana. The national airline, the agricultural marketing board, Botswana Meat Commission, Botswana Telecommunications Corporation, Bank of Botswana, Botswana Development Corporation and the postal services are identified as having potential for takeover by the private sector.
